_comment: Homeowner-equity-weighted town list for secured loan and second charge location pages. Deliberately close to the INVERSE of landlordCities.json: secured borrowing needs mortgaged owner-occupiers with equity, which means commuter and suburban towns, not the northern rental cities that suit buy-to-let refinance. Research and sourcing: docs/secured-loan-cities-research.md. Every town listed already has a bridging location page. Not yet wired into any seeder.

tiers.label: Southern commuter belt — peak mortgaged ownership
tiers.rationale: The local authorities with the highest share of households owning with a mortgage are all in the south or east: Wokingham 42.0%, Dartford 41.0%, Hart 40.2%, Bracknell Forest 39.7%, Central Bedfordshire 39.3%. Mortgaged owner-occupiers with equity are exactly the second charge market. The South East also holds the highest median household wealth in Britain at £503,400, most of it property.

tiers.label: Scotland and the Central Belt — home market
tiers.rationale: Boxx is Coatbridge-based, and Lanarkshire and the wider Central Belt are owner-occupier territory with modest prices and long tenure. Lower absolute equity than the South East, but a local broker has an advantage here that it does not have in Surrey. Scottish secured lending also differs in process — standard securities rather than legal charges — so the copy must not simply be an English page renamed.

tiers.label: Regional cities and market towns with settled ownership
tiers.rationale: Mid-priced towns with high owner-occupation, established equity and enough population to generate volume. Weaker per-lead value than tier 1 but far less competitive, and several are places where a specialist broker can rank quickly.
